question: How can a nurse manager best handle frequent equipment shortages during daily ward activities?

question: Why is comprehensive sexuality education more effective than just telling teens to practice abstinence?

question: Why should you place dentures back in a patient's mouth before family viewing, unless policy says otherwise?

question: Why should you use a clean spatula or tongue depressor when taking cream from a shared jar?

question: What is the primary purpose of isolation in a hospital setting?

question: Why do nurses keep their feet wide apart when lifting a patient?

question: What is the main job of the 'memory cells' created when someone gets vaccinated?

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand water microbiology?

question: Why do modern nurses prefer keeping a wound environment moist?

question: If your rural clinic runs out of official safety boxes, what is a safe, clever backup plan for used needles?

question: What usually causes recall bias when patients fill out questionnaires?

options.D: Patients forgetting past events or giving socially desirable answers

question: Where must a urinary catheter collection bag be positioned at all times to prevent backflow?

question: When is it safe for the transport nurse to leave the patient at the receiving hospital?

question: What do we mean by "abnormal illness behaviour"?

question: In simple terms, what does 'demand' mean when we talk about health services?

question: Before giving a drug, you use a bedside tool to scan both the patient's wristband and the medication. What is this safety tool called?

question: Where is patient data kept in an on-premise EHR setup?

question: Why is 'replication' (repeating a study) so important in scientific nursing research?

question: Why are electrical toys not allowed inside or near an oxygen tent?

question: What is the primary purpose of a downward referral in mental health?

question: Why is this special fund called 'revolving'?

options.D: Sinus bradycardia

question: What is a common consequence of mental health stigma in many communities?

options.C: People hide their symptoms and delay seeking professional help
options.D: Traditional healers refuse to communicate with psychiatric nurses

question: Why can relying too much on assistive technology become a problem in patient care?

options.C: It forces patients to perform rigorous physical exercises
options.D: It eliminates the need for any future medical research

explanation: You're doing great! While tech is helpful, leaning on machines too much can cut down on the warm, meaningful human contact patients need. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to avoid bias when picking patients for a study?

options.A: Hand-picking only the friendliest patients to answer questionnaires
options.B: Clearly defining inclusion and exclusion rules before starting
options.C: Ensuring that diverse patient sub-groups are properly represented

explanation: You're doing great! Hand-picking only your favorite or friendliest patients introduces bias because it doesn't give everyone a fair and equal chance to participate. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h6)

question: A patient with frequent malaria infections lives in a neighborhood with stagnant drainage water and poor housing. Which factor is most directly influencing this patient's health?

options.A: A lack of personal interest in health education
options.B: An unavoidable genetic predisposition to mosquito bites
options.C: Environmental and social determinants of health
options.D: An acute psychological response to stress

question: What is the main reason for routine health checkups before hiring food handlers?

options.A: To detect communicable diseases before workers start preparing food
options.B: To assess how well workers can handle high-stress kitchen environments
options.C: To determine the correct salary grade for each new kitchen employee
options.D: To test the physical strength and endurance of kitchen staff

explanation: Screenings catch infectious illnesses early so sick or asymptomatic workers don't spread germs to customers. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h4)

question: What does a survivor-centric approach in nursing care prioritize above all else?

options.A: Public awareness campaigns in local newspapers
options.B: The survivor's rights, wishes, safety, and confidentiality
options.C: The hospital's administrative reporting deadlines
options.D: Immediate arrest of the suspect regardless of consent

explanation: A survivor-centric model puts the autonomy and emotional safety of the patient at the center of every decision. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h6)

question: A mum who delivered an hour ago at a primary clinic has soaked three maternity pads in 30 minutes and feels dizzy. What's going on?

options.A: An impending eclamptic seizure
options.B: Normal postpartum lochia flow
options.C: A normal physiological recovery sign
options.D: Primary postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Soaking pads rapidly plus dizziness means heavy bleeding (PPH). She needs quick intervention right away! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h2)

question: What is the big advantage of an enterprise EHR system in a large health network?

options.A: It connects multiple hospitals and clinics into a single shared database
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to document patient assessments
options.C: It completely replaces the need for doctors in outpatient clinics
options.D: It automatically lowers the cost of prescription drugs for patients

explanation: Correct! Enterprise systems tie various hospitals and clinics together so patient files travel smoothly across the whole network. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT part of a nurse's everyday clinical responsibilities?

options.A: Educating the community on the importance of immunization
options.B: Synthesizing laboratory antibodies in a research facility
options.C: Monitoring patients for adverse reactions after vaccination
options.D: Recognizing early clinical signs of an allergic reaction

explanation: Growing and building antibodies in a lab is work for researchers and scientists. Nurses focus on patient care, safety, and community health education! [learn more](GST114_U4_T1#GST114_U4_T1_h9)

question: Why is the brain hit the hardest when someone experiences asphyxia?

options.A: It has a high metabolic rate and constant oxygen demand
options.B: It produces its own oxygen through cellular division
options.C: It stores large reserves of backup oxygen
options.D: It is protected by cerebrospinal fluid that blocks toxins

explanation: The brain is a busy organ that constantly demands oxygen. When that supply cuts off, brain cells start struggling almost immediately. Great job reviewing this! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T6#GNS221_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the immediate nursing action if a chemical splashes into a patient's eyes?

options.A: Wait for laboratory blood test results before touching the face
options.B: Cover the eyes tightly with dry gauze bandages without washing
options.C: Flush the eyes continuously with clean water for at least fifteen minutes
options.D: Apply concentrated acid neutralizer drops directly to the corneas

explanation: Spot on! Quick and long flushing with clean water washes the chemical away before it can permanently damage the cornea. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h5)

question: What is the term for a piece of dead bone separated from living bone during osteomyelitis?

options.A: Cortex
options.B: Involucrum
options.C: Callus
options.D: Sequestrum

explanation: A sequestrum is the segment of necrotic bone that has lost its blood supply due to severe infection and pressure. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of essential drugs in a healthcare system?

options.A: To replace all traditional remedies in rural communities
options.B: To provide experimental treatments for rare chronic illnesses
options.C: To generate maximum revenue for local pharmaceutical companies
options.D: To satisfy the priority health care needs of the population

explanation: Essential drugs are specifically chosen because they target the most common and urgent health conditions affecting a community. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is it important for the family to have a direct contact number for the psychiatric ward during a patient's leave?

options.A: So they can order extra hospital meals to be delivered
options.B: So they can negotiate a discount on hospital bills
options.C: So they can seek immediate guidance before minor challenges escalate into major crises
options.D: So they can report local weather conditions to the doctor

explanation: Having a direct phone line gives families peace of mind and lets them get professional advice before small issues become big problems. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h7)

question: Which of these makes a research hypothesis weak and unusable?

options.A: Matching the primary research question too closely
options.B: Being based on existing nursing theory
options.C: Predicting a negative relationship between variables
options.D: Using vague terms that cannot be measured

explanation: Keep it clear! If words are too fuzzy to measure, researchers won't be able to collect real data to check if it's true. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T10#GNS217_U3_T10_h2)

question: Why is the IASC framework designed as a pyramid rather than a square?

options.A: To illustrate that basic community needs affect a larger population than specialized care
options.B: To prove that physical safety is less important than psychiatric medications
options.C: To show that specialized services are needed by the majority of the population
options.D: To demonstrate that doctors must handle every level of community distress

explanation: Think of it like a crowd: the wide base at the bottom represents everyday survival needs that affect almost everyone, while the narrow top shows specialized care needed by fewer people. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T5#GNS314_U6_T5_h1)

question: An adult female patient refuses a procedure, but her husband insists you must do it anyway. What should you do?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately without explanation
options.B: Obey the husband because he is the head of the household
options.C: Respect the patient's autonomous refusal and maintain her confidentiality
options.D: Perform the procedure secretly without the patient knowing

explanation: Every competent adult has the final say over her own body. A patient's right to refuse always overrides outside family demands. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h4)

question: If a seriously ill child has a completely normal blood pressure reading, does that mean they are out of danger?

options.A: Fluid resuscitation is definitely not needed
options.B: The child is completely free from danger
options.C: Cardiac output is at its absolute maximum
options.D: The child may still be in compensated shock

explanation: Kids are amazing at squeezing their blood vessels tight to keep their blood pressure looking normal, even when they are crashing. A normal BP doesn't mean they aren't in shock! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why do nurses track balancing measures during an improvement project?

options.A: To detect any unintended negative consequences in other parts of the system
options.B: To compare the hospital performance against international standards
options.C: To balance the nursing unit's monthly financial budget and payroll
options.D: To ensure that doctors and nurses work the exact same number of hours

explanation: Brilliant! Balancing measures act like an early warning system to make sure fixing one problem doesn't accidentally cause another one somewhere else. [learn more](GST319_U3_T1#GST319_U3_T1_h4)

question: How does keeping your muscles tense for too long due to poor posture affect your body?

options.A: It builds permanent muscle mass faster than regular exercise
options.B: It increases the oxygen supply to the overworked muscle fibers
options.C: It cools down the body temperature in surrounding joints
options.D: It reduces adequate blood flow, leading to fatigue and pain

explanation: Spot on! Constant muscle tension squeezes your blood vessels, starving your muscles of oxygen and leaving you feeling sore and tired. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why is 'operational scalability' so important for a Rapid Response Center?

options.A: It allows the center to expand or shrink its response as the emergency changes
options.B: It prevents staff members from ever working overtime shifts
options.C: It ensures that all patients receive identical care regardless of injury severity
options.D: It guarantees that funding will never run out during a crisis

explanation: Emergencies change fast. Scalability means the center can ramp up gear and staff when things get worse, or scale down safely when things calm down. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h2)

question: Why should you avoid heavy medical jargon when teaching a family caregiver?

options.A: It increases the cost of home care equipment
options.B: It makes the nurse look uneducated
options.C: Medical terms are illegal to use outside of hospitals
options.D: It prevents the caregiver from understanding how to safely manage care

question: What do we call the medical measurement of the inside of a woman's pelvis to check if she can deliver vaginally?

question: Why is preventing hypothermia so crucial when treating trauma victims?

options.A: It prevents the need for any intravenous fluids.

options.C: Cold bodies cause blood clotting mechanisms to fail and worsen bleeding.
options.D: Hypothermia makes patients sleep through their injuries.

question: A nurse sits quietly in the corner of a pediatric playroom to watch children interact without joining in or altering the setting. What kind of observation is this?

options.B: Non-participant observation
options.C: Unstructured clinical interview

question: When should respiratory hygiene measures start for a patient visiting the hospital?

options.D: Only after a doctor confirms a respiratory diagnosis

question: What is a common reason why teenagers avoid visiting reproductive health clinics?

options.D: Mandatory waiting periods exceeding one full month

question: Which type of hospital structure features a long, top-down chain of command with many layers of management?

options.D: Informal structure

question: In Nigerian homes, which household liquid is most often accidentally swallowed by children because it's stored in empty drink bottles?

question: What is usually the main symptom of a small, uninfected vulval cyst?

question: What legal document outlines a patient's specific wishes regarding life-sustaining medical treatments?

question: Why is strict waste segregation vital during home visits?

question: How does living in an unstable housing environment negatively affect a person's emotional health?

question: A maternity ward wants to stop unauthorized movement of newborns. Which technology is most useful?

question: Why is actively sharing research so important for everyday nursing practice?

question: Why are balancing measures important when implementing a new nursing procedure?

question: What do nurses need to do periodically to renew their practicing licenses?

question: A community has non-English speakers and residents with hearing impairments. How should you adapt the emergency warning system?

question: What is a great, simple first step a nurse can suggest to an overweight teenager looking to improve their diet?

question: A resident needs physical help to cut their food and bring it to their mouth. Which daily living activity does this fall under?

question: What is the main purpose of the Minimum Data Set (MDS) assessment tool in a skilled nursing facility?

question: Which sign is a nurse most likely to notice in a newborn with an open heart shunt like PDA?

question: What are the three core action steps when giving Psychological First Aid (PFA)?

question: If a ward suddenly admits many new patients and uses up way more syringes and IV fluids, how are these supplies classed?

question: What is the main goal of taking proactive steps to manage conflict antecedents?

question: What should you do first if a smart bed's motorized controls stop working?

options.B: Check the power supply and ensure control lockouts are off

question: A client says she still takes her birth control pill every day, but admits she forgets it at least three times a week. How would you describe this?

options.C: Poor continuation and no compliance

question: A patient is given a drug that stimulates beta-2 receptors. What body change do you expect?

question: When a QA committee checks patient files (chart audits), what are they mostly looking for?

question: What is the main goal of giving medications for chronic, degenerative diseases like Parkinson's or Alzheimer's?

options.A: To manage ongoing physical and mental decline

options.C: To permanently stop the normal aging process
options.D: To wipe out sudden bacterial infections in the tissues

explanation: You've got this! Because degenerative diseases cause gradual wear and tear on the body, medications are used to slow things down and help patients manage daily life, rather than providing a quick cure. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h1)

question: What usually causes conductive hearing loss?

options.D: Damage to the vestibulocochlear nerve

question: Beyond treating patients, what is an essential public health task for a nurse on an international disaster team?

options.B: Auditing the international bank accounts of the United Nations
options.C: Negotiating ceasefire agreements between warring military factions
options.D: Purchasing international commercial airline tickets for arriving staff

question: What is a key nursing action immediately following an ophthalmoscopy exam where dilating drops were used?

options.D: Ensuring the patient has safe transportation home due to blurred vision

question: Which simple nursing care measure helps soothe irritated vulval tissue and keep the area clean?

options.C: Applying dry heat packs directly to the skin

question: How does a traditional "blame culture" usually handle mistakes in a hospital?

question: Why is clearing away rubble and setting up temporary ramps so vital inside a disaster relief camp?

options.B: It replaces the need for medical triage stations
options.C: It completely stops the spread of waterborne diseases
options.D: It is required before anyone is allowed to eat

question: Why are exclusion criteria inside a standing order just as important as inclusion criteria?

options.A: They reduce the amount of paperwork the nurse needs to fill out at the end of the shift

options.C: They tell the pharmacist how many tablets of each medication to dispense
options.D: They help identify warning signs that mean the patient is too sick for routine protocol treatment

explanation: Exclusion criteria flag danger signs or complications that require immediate referral rather than standard clinic treatment. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h4)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when starting a Behavioural Change Communication project?

options.A: Evaluating final program financial costs

options.C: Assessment and formative research
options.D: Mass media television broadcasting

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance at local health centers during an outbreak?

options.B: To detect suspected cases early and prevent widespread transmission
options.C: To test every healthy citizen in the town for virus antibodies
options.D: To force all community members to stay indoors under quarantine

explanation: Exactly! Spotting sick people early lets healthcare teams jump in fast and stop the outbreak from spreading. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h8)

question: A community health nurse organizes a blood pressure screening exercise at the local market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Primary prevention
options.B: Primordial prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Screenings are designed for early detection of health problems so that intervention can start before complications develop. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why do people trying to quit smoking often get sudden cravings when doing routine things, like drinking morning tea?

options.A: Their physical lungs are suddenly damaged by the beverage steam
options.B: The brain has formed strong behavioral links between those routines and smoking
options.C: Their immune system is reacting to dietary changes
options.D: The tea contains hidden traces of chemical nicotine

explanation: Daily habits act as triggers because the brain links those routines directly to smoking. Recognizing this helps us support patients better! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h4)

question: What should you tell a patient who has a normal routine EEG result, but a clear history of seizures?

options.A: The patient's seizures have spontaneously resolved without medical intervention
options.B: A normal EEG does not rule out epilepsy because abnormal waves may not occur during a short test
options.C: The testing equipment was likely calibrated incorrectly during the procedure
options.D: Further neurological evaluation is unnecessary once a normal EEG is recorded

explanation: Routine EEGs only record a short snapshot in time. Many people with true epilepsy have completely normal EEGs between their seizure episodes! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T9#GNS222_U4_T9_h5)

question: A patient on the ward has a normal blood pressure but a rising heart rate and an increased breathing rate. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The room temperature is simply too high.
options.B: The patient is recovering well and ready for discharge.
options.C: The patient is compensating for an early internal complication.
options.D: The monitoring equipment needs to be replaced immediately.

explanation: Changes in heart and breathing rates are early distress signals that show up before blood pressure finally gives way. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of rehabilitation services for special children?

options.A: To keep the child confined to a hospital bed
options.B: To eliminate the need for any assistive technology
options.C: To completely cure all genetic and congenital disorders
options.D: To maximize independence and improve quality of life

explanation: Rehabilitation focuses on helping children function at their highest possible level despite chronic limitations. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h5)

question: What does 'precision' measure in an information retrieval search?

options.A: The percentage of articles written by registered nurses
options.B: The proportion of retrieved documents that are actually relevant
options.C: The total number of seconds the computer takes to search
options.D: The exact number of spelling errors found in the abstract

explanation: Precision evaluates how well your search weeded out useless results, telling you what percentage of what you found was truly useful. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h6)

question: A mosquito develops through an egg, larva, pupa, and winged adult. Which type of metamorphosis does this represent?

options.A: Simple metamorphosis
options.B: Incomplete metamorphosis
options.C: Complete metamorphosis
options.D: Direct development

explanation: Because it features four separate stages including a resting pupa, it is classified as complete metamorphosis. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h3)

question: Which layer of the skin has the highest number of specialized touch receptors?

options.A: Dermis
options.B: Stratum corneum
options.C: Epidermis
options.D: Subcutaneous adipose

explanation: Great job! The dermis sits right beneath the outer layer and houses most of those complex touch and pressure receptors. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T5#GNS211_U4_T5_h2)

question: Which of these common patient habits is a major driver of antimicrobial resistance?

options.A: Taking prescribed antiviral medications for severe fungal skin rashes
options.B: Storing leftover medications in a cool, dark hospital refrigerator
options.C: Stopping prescribed antibiotic courses early before all bacteria are killed
options.D: Washing hands too frequently with standard antibacterial liquid soap

explanation: When patients stop antibiotics early, the toughest bacteria survive, multiply, and learn how to beat the drug next time! [learn more](GST114_U3_T2#GST114_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why is knowing the stages of the Transtheoretical Model useful for a clinical nurse?

options.A: It accurately predicts the exact day a patient will stop smoking or exercising
options.B: It helps tailor counselling to match the patient's exact readiness to change
options.C: It proves whether a patient has a genetic predisposition to chronic illness
options.D: It replaces the need for physical assessments during routine clinic visits

explanation: Exactly right! People change at their own pace. Knowing their stage helps you meet them where they are instead of pushing too hard too fast. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T15#GNS313_U3_T15_h3)

question: How do vaccines effectively interrupt the chain of infection within a community?

options.A: By chemically sterilizing the drinking water supply in rural areas
options.B: By destroying all bacteria living on hospital furniture and walls
options.C: By creating immunity in susceptible hosts so germs cannot find vulnerable people
options.D: By preventing nurses from carrying pathogens on their uniforms

explanation: Immunizing individuals removes the susceptible host link, halting the spread of disease through herd immunity. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h6)

question: What is the main job of the Bartholin's glands?

options.A: To secrete mucus for lubrication
options.B: To produce the female egg cells
options.C: To maintain acidic vaginal pH
options.D: To filter waste from the blood

explanation: Correct! These glands release fluid to keep the vaginal opening lubricated. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T1#GNS121_U5_T1_h5)
